nodes.label: The recommended hand positions are nine-and-three or eight-and-four on the steering wheel, with thumbs and knuckles kept outside the wheel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Use hand-to-hand steering for modest changes and hand-over-hand steering when a larger steering movement is needed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: At an intersection, the vehicle approaching from the left yields to the vehicle on its right unless an official control or police direction establishes a different rule.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: A left-turning driver must yield to opposing traffic already in the intersection or close enough to present an immediate hazard.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Right-of-way rules guide yielding decisions, but a driver must still assess the actual intersection rather than assume an automatic entitlement to proceed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: For an emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights from any direction, move promptly to the right edge and stop without blocking the intersection.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After an emergency vehicle passes, signal and return to the roadway only once the movement is safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Yield to the driver who reached the intersection first, and at a simultaneous four-way-stop arrival yield to the driver on the right.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When joining a public highway from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the highway.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Traffic entering a limited-access highway or interstate must yield to vehicles already traveling on that highway.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Allow pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles already inside an intersection to finish passing through.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Yield to a funeral procession and allow its headlight-using vehicles following the hearse to pass together.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Choose a speed that accounts for the road, visibility, traffic and vehicle condition while keeping the vehicle under full control.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A speed limit describes the greatest permitted speed for ideal conditions, rather than a requirement to maintain that speed in every situation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The manual gives a thirty-mile-per-hour maximum for a business district or urban residential district as defined in the cited statute.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The stated thirty-five-mile-per-hour maximum applies to defined rural residential districts and specified Class V highways outside a municipality's compact area.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook lists forty-five or fifty-five miles per hour for other locations, with separately stated exceptions for certain divided highways and the specified Interstate ninety-three segment.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The stated sixty-five-mile-per-hour category covers the interstate system and the named central and eastern turnpikes where they are divided highways with at least four lanes.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook gives seventy miles per hour for Interstate ninety-three between mile marker forty-five and the Vermont border.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The interstate minimum is forty-five miles per hour unless road or weather conditions make that speed unsafe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Driving far below the normal traffic flow can create a hazard by obstructing others and encouraging risky passing or lane changes.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: In a posted school zone, reduce the usual limit by ten miles per hour during the forty-five minutes preceding opening and the forty-five minutes after closing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A turn should be signaled at least one hundred feet beforehand, while a highway lane change or exit should be signaled at least five hundred feet beforehand.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Signal a turn earlier when rain, snow or fog increases other vehicles' stopping-distance needs.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use the appropriate turn signal for turns, lane changes, highway entries or exits, driveway entry, merging, curb departure, pulling over and passing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A passenger vehicle needs at least two front lamps lit from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use the required front lamps when rain, snow or fog prevents a clear view of people and vehicles one thousand feet ahead.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use a horn when communication with another road user requires it, because inappropriate horn use can startle or anger others.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not sound the horn near a blind pedestrian or a horse, since frightening the horse can lead to a crash.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: An ordinary warning generally needs only a light horn tap.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A light horn warning may help when a pedestrian or bicyclist enters your lane, another driver moves into it, or a backing driver has not noticed your approach.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Stopping distance includes travel from recognizing a need to stop until the vehicle becomes stationary under the stated ideal conditions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A higher traveling speed requires additional stopping time and distance.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Perception time is the interval needed to recognize that stopping is necessary; the handbook gives an alert-driver average of three-quarters of a second through one second.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reaction time includes moving the foot off the accelerator and onto the brake, with a stated average of three-quarters of a second through one second.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The braking-distance example says that at fifty miles per hour on dry pavement, good brakes can still require approximately one hundred fifty-eight feet to stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Maintain at least a four-second following gap, and avoid following more closely than reasonable conditions permit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When another driver follows dangerously close, find a safe place to pull aside and allow that driver to pass.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before a lane change, examine mirrors, check blind spots directly, identify a gap, signal and look again before adjusting speed and steering into the new lane.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use a highway acceleration lane to approach the speed of existing traffic, select an opening and merge into the flow.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Prepare for an exit early by moving toward the appropriate lane without a sudden lane change.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep roadway speed on the main carriageway, then signal, enter the deceleration lane and slow for its posted exit speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Pass only where signs or markings permit it and road conditions make the maneuver suitable.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not attempt a pass with approaching opposing traffic, restricted sight around a hill or curve, at an intersection, or before a railroad crossing or bridge.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On a multilane road the far-left lane is intended for passing slower traffic; a shoulder must never be used for passing, whether paved or unpaved.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Estimate enough time and room to complete a pass without interfering with another vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before passing, check opposing traffic, mirrors and blind spots; signal and move smoothly into the passing lane when safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Remain in the passing lane until the entire front of the overtaken vehicle can be seen in the rearview mirror, then signal and return smoothly.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When another vehicle passes, hold your lane and a steady speed, and never accelerate to prevent the pass.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before entering the vehicle to back up, inspect the space behind it for children and objects hidden from the driver's seating position.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Mirrors and head checks do not reveal every part of the area immediately behind the vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Back slowly with gentle acceleration and small steering inputs toward the direction the rear should travel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When backing through a turn, briefly check front and sides while continuing to look rearward until the vehicle stops completely.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A rear camera supplements mirrors and proper head checks; it should not become the primary means of checking behind the vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Slow to an appropriate speed before entering a curve and reduce speed further for poor traction, following traffic or an unseen curve exit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Hard braking after entering a curve can cause tires to lose grip.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At the first signs of rain, snow, sleet or ice, reduce speed because weaker tire grip makes stopping and turning more difficult.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Hydroplaning occurs when the steering tires ride on pooled water instead of maintaining road contact.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reduce hydroplaning risk by slowing in rain or pooled water and maintaining sufficient tire tread and proper tire pressure.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Choose another route rather than driving through a flooded road or a large accumulation of standing water.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On gravel or dirt, slow down, leave more space ahead and expect possible skidding while stopping.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: On a narrow rural road, reduce speed, keep centered in your own travel lane and watch for approaching vehicles encroaching into it.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Watch narrow-bridge warnings and take turns on a single-lane bridge; generally the first driver to reach it proceeds first.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Steel bridges or open gratings can weaken traction, calling for lower speed, greater following room and a secure grip on the wheel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Where vegetation, hills or blind corners restrict sight, reduce speed and remain prepared to stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Approach an uncontrolled rural intersection cautiously, slowing and preparing to stop for crossing or opposing traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Night driving is more hazardous because available headlight illumination limits how far the driver can see.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: High beams may be used when there is no opposing traffic, but dim them for approaching vehicles and use low beams behind another vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use low beams in fog, rain or snow because high-beam glare can make forward vision worse.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If approaching headlights dazzle you, direct your gaze toward the right road edge rather than looking into the lights.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Scan ahead for dark silhouettes and glance toward both road edges for hazards approaching from the sides.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid tinted or colored lenses at night or on overcast days because they reduce vision.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Increase following time by at least one second at night, or by at least two seconds on an unfamiliar road at night.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Warning technologies commonly provide sound, light or vibration alerts without automatically preventing a collision or fault.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Treat driver-assistance warnings as added support for mirrors and direct head checks, never as a replacement for active monitoring.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When backing, monitor side mirrors, the interior mirror, direct over-shoulder views and any fitted camera.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A reversing camera activates when reverse is selected and displays the area behind the vehicle on the vehicle's screen.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A backup warning system scans behind the vehicle in reverse and may use sound, vibration or both to indicate an obstruction.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A blind-spot monitor may assist a lane change, but the driver must still check mirrors and look over the shoulder.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A curve-speed warning alerts the driver when the approach to a curve or exit is too fast.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A surround-view monitor combines overhead and nearby views of the vehicle and may add sonar warnings about nearby obstructions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Forward-collision warning scans ahead and alerts the driver about a slower or stationary vehicle or object; that warning alone does not apply the brakes.
